ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 2 — Focused Visit (Follow-up) — Jesse Owens

code.originalText: Diagnosis of left upper lobe adenocarcinoma, stage IIB: thoracic oncology consultation, tumor board plan for chemoimmunotherapy before surgery, and start of varenicline

text.paragraph: Diagnosis visit: staging and biopsy results, the tumor board plan, and the thoracic oncology consultation. [S]

Mr. Owens returns two weeks after the screening CT. PET-CT three days after the scan showed the 2.9 cm left upper lobe nodule and a left interlobar node to be active, with nothing in the mediastinum or elsewhere, and brain MRI the next day was clear. Endobronchial ultrasound a week ago found adenocarcinoma in the interlobar node, with four other node stations negative. PD-L1 is 40 percent, and tissue sequencing, back yesterday, shows a KRAS G12C mutation and no EGFR, ALK or other targetable alteration. The thoracic tumor board reviewed him five days ago. He had pulmonary function tests this morning and saw Dr. Halvorsen-Pierce at midday. He still has his usual morning cough, no breathlessness, and has lost no weight. He is still smoking a pack a day and now wants to stop: the scan has convinced him. He has had no thoughts of self-harm. [S]

text.paragraph: Vital signs recorded on 2026-05-26; see the Vital Signs section. [S]

tr.td: Well and upright; weight 76.6 kg; blood pressure 130/80, pulse 80; oxygen saturation 95 percent
Breath sounds equal; scattered early-morning rhonchi that clear with a cough; no wheeze
Regular rhythm; no murmur; no edema
Attentive, asks direct questions and writes the answers down

Solid, spiculated 2.9 cm nodule in the left upper lobe with an enlarged (1.6 cm) left hilar lymph node on today's low-dose screening CT, Lung-RADS 4X (very suspicious); no symptoms of lung cancer. PET-CT, tissue diagnosis and thoracic oncology review booked
S — Synthetic presenting screening finding in a long-term smoker. Superseded by the diagnosis at the second visit.

Adenocarcinoma of the left upper lobe of the lung, cT1c N1 M0, stage IIB (AJCC 8th edition), resectable: 2.9 cm primary with a positive left interlobar (11L) node on EBUS; mediastinal nodes 4R, 4L and 7 negative; no metastases on PET-CT or brain MRI. PD-L1 tumor proportion score 40 percent (22C3); KRAS G12C mutation; no EGFR, ALK, ROS1, BRAF, MET exon 14, RET, NTRK or HER2 alteration
S — Synthetic histology, stage and biomarkers linked to his documented adenocarcinoma of the left lung; in the modern episode it is found by screening while still resectable.
Nicotine dependence, cigarettes: a pack a day for 35 years (35 pack-years); smokes his first cigarette within 30 minutes of waking; two attempts to stop, each lasting a few weeks without medicine
S — Synthetic modern entry linked to his documented smoking; superseded at the visit after surgery by nicotine dependence in early remission.

list.item:
Adenocarcinoma of the left upper lobe, cT1c N1 M0, stage IIB (C34.12). Non-small cell lung cancer found by his first screening CT while it can still be cured. Systematic EBUS staging shows hilar (N1) but not mediastinal spread, and PET-CT and brain MRI show no metastases. Because there is no EGFR or ALK alteration, nivolumab with platinum chemotherapy before surgery is an option that improves event-free survival and the chance of a complete pathologic response over surgery first, and the tumor board and Dr. Halvorsen-Pierce recommend it. His lung function allows a lobectomy (predicted postoperative FEV1 and DLCO both 63 percent). The KRAS G12C result does not change treatment now, but is kept for any recurrence. [S]
Cycle 1 of nivolumab, carboplatin and pemetrexed in eight days, on his chosen quit date.
Hepatitis B, hepatitis C and HIV tests drawn today.
Folic acid from today and vitamin B12 injection today; dexamethasone around each cycle.
Baseline thyroid, cortisol, liver and kidney tests today.
Restaging CT after cycle 3; thoracic surgery review before then.
PCV20 given today, before treatment.

Nicotine dependence, cigarettes (F17.210). Ready to quit now. Stopping smoking after a lung cancer diagnosis lowers surgical complications and improves survival, so it is part of his cancer treatment. Varenicline is the most effective single medicine; no history of seizures or mood disorder, and his kidney function is normal. [S]
Varenicline 0.5 mg daily for three days, then twice daily, then 1 mg twice daily from day 8.
Quit date on day 1 of cycle 1.
Quitline enrollment today; counseling at every visit.

Lung-RADS 4X nodule (R91.1). Explained by the diagnosis made today; superseded. [S]
Problem resolved.
